question.text:
The reaction

$\mathrm{MgO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}),$ for which

$\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}=+491.1 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}=198.0 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

is not feasible at $298 \mathrm{~K}$. Temperature above which reaction will be feasible is

solution.text:
$\mathrm{MgO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$

For a reaction to be spontaneous $\Delta \mathrm{G}  < 0$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ} < 0$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}>\frac{\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}}{\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}}$

$\mathrm{T}>\frac{491.1 \times 1000}{198}$

$\mathrm{T}>2480.3 \mathrm{~K}$
